idiom_name: Akka Typed / Pekko Typed Actors (Behavior + ActorRef)
implementation_notes: Scala is the language the JVM actor ecosystem grew up in: Akka Typed - and its Apache-2.0 fork Pekko after the license change - makes the actor a Behavior[Msg] function and the address an ActorRef[Msg], while the ActorSystem owns mailboxes and dispatchers. State is threaded functionally: each message returns the next behavior (Behaviors.same when nothing changes), so the classic mutable actor object is replaced by an immutable behavior plus a typed protocol, and supervision is declared with Behaviors.supervise rather than written as try/catch. Choose it when actors are the application's architecture (clustering, sharding, streams, persistence); for one mailbox a channel or queue is simpler.
pitfalls: A sealed message hierarchy lets the compiler check the protocol; widening messages to Any throws that away and defeats typed actors.
Blocking inside the default dispatcher starves every actor scheduled on it; assign blocking work its own dispatcher or wrap it in a future.
Returning Behaviors.stopped deliberately ends the actor and sends later messages to dead letters; omitting it leaves the actor running, so make termination a visible protocol transition.
Newer Akka versions are BUSL-1.1 licensed; Pekko is the Apache-2.0 fork when the license matters.
